title: Cooking with attention
hook: Brother Lawrence disliked kitchen work, yet said he found God there as on his knees
tomorrow: should you sweep the floor for God, or just sweep the floor?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Marcus at the start of the day: they're having a day, and they're still kin. Today, a man who found his whole practice in the room he liked least.
screen: `THEY'RE HAVING A DAY.` → `THE ROOM HE LIKED LEAST.`

segments.voice: Cooking videos make the kitchen look like a spa: slow knives, warm light, soft music. Here's a stranger kitchen. Brother Lawrence was a lay brother among the Carmelites, sent to work as a cook. By his own account he had a great natural aversion to kitchen work. And yet he said that in the noise and clatter of his kitchen, with several people asking him for different things at once, he possessed God as calmly as if he were on his knees before the Blessed Sacrament. A man who disliked the kitchen, calling it as good as the altar. How?
screen: `KITCHENS LIKE SPAS.` → `A COOK WHO DISLIKED COOKING.` → `GOD IN THE CLATTER.` → `HOW?`

segments.voice: His answer had a plain name: the practice of the presence of God. He didn't wait for prayer time to pray. He talked with God simply, while doing whatever was in front of him, and when his mind wandered, he came back without fuss. He said God looks not at the greatness of the work but at the love it's done with, so even little things count. He would turn the cake frying in the pan for the love of God. That's the puzzle solved: he never had to like the kitchen. He only had to not be alone in it. This is a Christian practice, born among Catholic Carmelites, and this path borrows it with its source named. Cooking with attention, for Brother Lawrence, wasn't a technique for calm. It was company, and love, put into the smallest task. The onion can be chopped for the love of God, as he would, or for the person who'll eat it. Either way the attention isn't on the clock. It's on the pan.
screen: `THE PRACTICE OF THE PRESENCE OF GOD.` · `LOVE, NOT THE SIZE OF THE WORK.` · `THE CAKE TURNED FOR LOVE.` · `HE ONLY HAD TO NOT BE ALONE.` · then, large: `THE KITCHEN.`

segments.voice: If something to eat or drink is close by, take one slow bite or sip and stay with it all the way through: the smell, the warmth, the taste. If not, walk through the last thing you cooked in your mind, the sound in the pan, the steam. When your mind runs ahead, come back to the pan without fuss, the way Brother Lawrence did.
Cooking with attention: Brother Lawrence's kitchen, where even turning a cake was done for love. Small work, fully present.
Keep this one: the kitchen, as good as the altar for a man who disliked it. Day four of the plain ones.

howItsDone: Christians who follow Brother Lawrence practice the presence of God through the day, talking with God simply while they work; people on this path borrow the attention and the love in small tasks.
